newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK has first Eurasian bone marrow register.
newsitem.headline: HK has first Eurasian bone marrow register.

text.p: The world's first Eurasian bone marrow registry has been set up in Hong Kong and 70 people have signed up, the organiser said on Sunday.
The registry was prompted by the long hunt for a bone marrow for two-year-old Joshua Gillespie-Wong, who is suffering from leukaemia.
Joshua, whose father is Chinese and mother Scottish, is seeking a perfect match for his rare bone marrow.
"Before yesterday there was no Eurasian bone marrow registry, but there is now," Carol Underwood, the campaign's organiser and friend of the family, told Hong Kong government radio.
Tests would be conducted on the 70 people to see whether their bone marrow would match Joshua's, Underwood said, adding that he was stable at the moment.
However, she stressed that he would need to find a suitable donor soon to have an operation.
